subject: Problem with data format exported from Skyline (version 3.1.0.7382 64-Bit)

messages.author: b818b9fd5701fbd8
messages.subject: Problem with data format exported from Skyline (version 3.1.0.7382 64-Bit)
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to analyze data from an MRM experiment with heavy labeled peptides using the MSstats R package (v 2.4.0) with data exported from Skyline. 

I know from your workflow examples that when you download the MSstats external tool package in Skyline, that you should be able to use the exported data from the "MSstats Input"document grid data from Skyline. However, I am having numerous issues with the data formatting that is exported (too many columns, incorrect colnames, outputs '#N/A' instead of 'NA', ect.).

Is there another way to export Skyline data for use in the R package? 

Thank you.

Jonathan Levi

messages.author: 99540594784b9805
messages.subject: Re: Problem with data format exported from Skyline (version 3.1.0.7382 64-Bit)
parts:
When you are exporting from Skyline, you should use the "File > Export > Report" menu item, and, on the Export Report dialog, choose "Invariant" in the Language dropdown.
If you export from the Document Grid, or if you don't choose "Invariant" for the language, then the column names will have spaces in them (e.g. "Fragment Ion")

The MSstats external tool does some processing on the data before calling the MSstats main functions.  You can see that code here:
https://svn.code.sf.net/p/proteowizard/code/trunk/pwiz/pwiz_tools/Skyline/Executables/Tools/MSstats/MSStatsGC.r

Here is some of the code which renames the "Area" and "FileName" columns:
# change column name as Intensity
colnames(raw)[colnames(raw)=="Area"]<-"Intensity"
raw$Intensity<-as.character(raw$Intensity)
raw$Intensity<-as.numeric(raw$Intensity)

# change column name 'FileName' as Run
colnames(raw)[colnames(raw)=="FileName"]<-"Run"


## impute zero to NA
#raw[!is.na(raw$Intensity)&raw$Intensity==0,"Intensity"]<-NA

I am not sure whether there is any other code that you would need to run in order to transform the Skyline report into what you need for your specific purpose.

Hope this helps,
-- Nick Shulman
MacCoss Lab, University of Washington
